title: A one-shot effect consumes its approval under the store lock
summary: An approval bound by a payload hash stops a replay only while the bound state differs; a one-shot effect must also consume the approval under the store lock, before the effect, and a test must reach that lock past any friendly pre-check.
hint_triggers: When an approved request authorizes a one-shot effect (archive, rebuild, grant, promotion), binding it to a payload hash is not enough: if the same state recurs, the hash matches again and the old approval would apply again. Call markApprovalConsumed with a literal consumer id before the effect, so the record lock refuses a second consumer and two concurrent applies cannot both run; a failed effect then needs a new approval. A pre-check that refuses a used approval gives a clear message but hides the lock from tests, so add a test where the consumer read the record before it was consumed (a stale read stand-in) and confirm by removing the consume that the tests fail. Keep the receipt and the consumption naming the same human decider.
